news.title: Agile Robots：融资5亿美元后估值达85亿美元
news.snippet: [该公司完成5亿美元融资，估值升至85亿美元，正从AI迈向Physical AI。]
news.raw_snippet:
## From Artificial Intelligence to Physical AI

Founded in 2018 as a spin-off from the German Aerospace Center (DLR), Agile Robots develops robotic systems that combine artificial intelligence, sensors and precision engineering.

Its products range from industrial robotic arms and dexterous hands to mobile and humanoid robots, supported by proprietary software and AI models. [...] The distinction between conventional automation and Physical AI is commercially significant. Traditional industrial robots generally perform predefined tasks in structured environments. AI-enabled systems aim to interpret changing conditions and adapt their behaviour accordingly.

That could open up more complex activities in manufacturing, logistics and electronics assembly, where tasks have historically depended on human dexterity and judgement. [...] The valuation reflects expectations about the commercial potential of Physical AI, but it reveals relatively little about the company’s underlying financial performance.

Agile Robots has not disclosed revenue, profitability or detailed financial terms in its funding announcement.

Without those figures, investors and industry observers cannot assess the valuation against sales, earnings or cash generation.

news.raw_snippet: In a press release from Public Citizen, attorney Matthew Platkin who filed the complaint on behalf of the plaintiffs said “It is patently illegal for companies to develop and release products they know are unsafe in any respect, let alone have the potential to exterminate the human race.
